﻿# EA Practice Governance Framework and Decision-Making Processes

**← Back to [EAP Home](../../README.md) • [Governance](../README.md)**

---

> This document defines the governance framework, processes, and decision-making structures for Gainwell's Enterprise Architecture Practice. It establishes clear processes, roles, and standards for architectural oversight, compliance, and continuous improvement to ensure the EA practice delivers value and maintains alignment with business objectives.

## 1.0 Governance Overview

Effective governance is essential to ensure that the Enterprise Architecture practice delivers value, maintains alignment with business objectives, and supports consistent decision-making across the organization. The governance approach establishes clear processes, roles, and standards for architectural oversight, compliance, and continuous improvement.
page_texts.4:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#11-purpose-and-scope]

### 1.1 Purpose and Scope

The EA governance framework serves to:

- **Ensure Alignment**: Maintain consistency between architectural decisions and business strategy
- **Manage Risk**: Identify and mitigate architectural and technical risks across the enterprise
- **Optimize Resources**: Coordinate architectural investments and avoid duplication
- **Maintain Standards**: Enforce architectural principles, standards, and best practices
- **Enable Innovation**: Balance standardization with innovation and emerging technology adoption
- **Support Compliance**: Ensure adherence to regulatory and industry requirements
page_texts.5:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#12-governance-principles]

### 1.2 Governance Principles

The governance approach is built on these [foundational principles](../../guiding-principles/core.md):

- **Business-Driven**: All architectural decisions must support business objectives and outcomes
- **Collaborative**: Inclusive decision-making process involving relevant stakeholders
- **Transparent**: Clear communication of decisions, rationale, and implementation plans
- **Agile**: Responsive governance that enables rapid adaptation to changing requirements
- **Risk-Informed**: Systematic risk assessment and mitigation planning
- **Continuous Improvement**: Regular evaluation and refinement of governance processes

---

## 2.0 Governance Process Framework

The governance framework implements a flexible multi-gate process integrated with GainwellNow (ServiceNow) to ensure systematic review, approval, and management of all enterprise architecture initiatives.
page_texts.7:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#21-gainwellnow-integration]

### 2.1 GainwellNow Integration

All governance processes are managed through GainwellNow (ServiceNow) to provide:

- **Centralized Intake**: Single point of entry for all project requests and initiatives
- **Automated Workflows**: Intelligent routing based on project characteristics and requirements
- **Progress Tracking**: Real-time visibility into governance process status and progress
- **Document Management**: Centralized repository for all governance artifacts and decisions
- **Reporting and Analytics**: Comprehensive reporting on governance effectiveness and performance
- **Audit Trail**: Complete audit trail of all decisions and approvals
- [GainwellNow Enterprise Architecture Governance](https://gainwellnow.service-now.com/esc?id=sc_cat_item&sys_id=3d2faedac356ce908978decf050131f6)
page_texts.8:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#22-flexible-gated-governance-process]

### 2.2 Flexible Gated Governance Process

The Gainwell EAP governance framework consists of multiple sequential gates, each with its own submission, review, and approval process. Each gate starts with a submission in GainwellNow and ends with either approval to proceed or remediation requirements. Gate 2 (Domain Review) and Gate 3 (Architecture Review Board) apply to project-based initiatives meeting the Medium/High risk, cross-domain, qualifying-activity threshold defined in the [Architecture Review Board Applicability](../governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#when-an-arb-input-form-is-required) section, as well as to any request independently mandated by an active enterprise standard, pattern, or governance policy under the standards-mandated path described in that same section; only requests meeting neither condition proceed directly from Logical Design to Build & Test. Within Gate 2, the Security Domain Review is mandatory whenever Gate 2/Gate 3 apply, while the AI Domain Review additionally applies only when the solution involves AI/ML.

### 2.3 Gate Requirements and Criteria

| Gate                              | Risk Level  | Data Sensitivity / Domain Impact  | Technology Impact                                           | Required    |
| --------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| Conceptual Review                 | All levels  | All types                          | New initiatives/major enhancements                          | Conditional |
| Domain Review                     | Medium/High | Cross-domain                       | Security (mandatory) and AI/ML requirements (if AI/ML)      | Conditional |
| Architecture Review Board         | Medium/High | Cross-domain                       | New technology/patterns/enterprise-wide/standard deviations | Conditional |
| Operational Readiness Test Review | All levels  | All production data                | All production systems                                      | Always      |
| Turnover to Operations Review     | All levels  | All production data                | All production systems                                      | Always      |
| Post Project Review               | All levels  | All types                          | All completed projects                                      | Always      |

page_texts.17:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#24-gainwellone-implementation-integration-flow]

### 2.4 GainwellOne Implementation Integration Flow

GainwellOne implementations follow a specialized governance flow that aligns with the standard enterprise architecture governance framework while accommodating the unique characteristics of the GainwellOne platform. This section outlines the implementation flow, key considerations, and integration points with the standard governance gates.

![Implementation Governance Flow](./assets/implmentation-governance.drawio.png)
page_texts.18:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#241-gainwellone-governance-integration-points]

#### 2.4.1 GainwellOne Governance Integration Points

GainwellOne implementations integrate with the standard governance framework at the following key points:

**Gate 1 - Conceptual Review**

- State-specific requirements analysis and feasibility assessment
- Regulatory and compliance requirement validation
- Platform customization vs. configuration decision points
- Initial security and privacy impact assessment

**Gate 2 - Domain Review**

- Specialized domain-specific review covering Security and AI/ML requirements

**Gate 3 - Architecture Review Board**

- Platform architecture alignment and customization review
- Integration architecture and interoperability patterns
- Data architecture and migration strategy
- Technology stack and platform version alignment

**Gate 4 - Operational Readiness Test**

- Platform configuration validation
- Multi-tenant deployment readiness
- Monitoring and alerting configuration
- Disaster recovery and business continuity validation

**Gate 5 - Turnover to Operations**

- Platform operations handoff procedures
- State-specific support requirements
- Knowledge transfer for platform customizations
- Operational runbook and escalation procedures

**Gate 6 - Post Project Review**

- Platform performance and scalability assessment
- Customization effectiveness evaluation
- Lessons learned for future implementations
- Platform improvement recommendations

---

[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#30-governance-bodies]

## 3.0 Governance Bodies

The governance framework includes multiple specialized review bodies with decision-making authority, each responsible for specific gates within the five-gate process. Detailed information about each governing body, including composition, responsibilities, entrance criteria, and processes, is documented in the [Governing Bodies](../governing-bodies/README.md) section.
page_texts.20:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#31-conceptual-review-board-crb]

### 3.1 Conceptual Review Board (CRB)

**Gate Authority**: Gate 1 - Conceptual Review Process

**Purpose**: Initial concept evaluation and strategic alignment assessment for new initiatives and projects entering the governance pipeline.

**Meeting Frequency**: Weekly

The CRB serves as the primary component of Gate 1, evaluating all new project concepts for strategic alignment, business value, and initial feasibility.

**See**: [Concept Review Board (CRB)](../governing-bodies/concept-review-board.md) for complete details on composition, responsibilities, entrance criteria, and review processes.
page_texts.21:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#32-domain-review-board-drb]

### 3.2 Domain Review Board (DRB)

**Gate Authority**: Gate 2 - Domain Review Process

**Purpose**: Specialized domain-specific reviews and validation covering Security and AI/ML requirements through adaptive composition.

**Meeting Frequency**: Weekly for regular reviews; Ad-hoc for urgent decisions

The DRB provides flexible, domain-specific governance through adaptive composition based on project needs, including security-focused and AI/ML-focused compositions.

**See**: [Domain Review Board (DRB)](../governing-bodies/domain-review-board.md) for complete details on adaptive composition model, meeting structures, entrance criteria, and review processes.
page_texts.22:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#33-architecture-review-board-arb]

### 3.3 Architecture Review Board (ARB)

**Gate Authority**: Gate 3 - Architecture Review Board Process

**Purpose**: Enterprise architecture alignment, design validation, and formal architectural approval for projects involving new technologies or significant enterprise impact.

**Meeting Frequency**: Weekly for regular reviews; Ad-hoc for urgent decisions

The ARB ensures alignment with enterprise strategy and adherence to architectural standards, reviewing solution architectures, technology selections, integration patterns, and compliance exceptions.

**See**: [Architecture Review Board (ARB)](../governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md) for complete details on composition, review processes, entrance criteria, and decision authority.
page_texts.23:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#34-operational-readiness-test-ort]

### 3.4 Operational Readiness Test (ORT)

**Gate Authority**: Gate 4 - Operational Readiness Test Process

**Purpose**: Production readiness validation and support procedures for all systems entering production environments.

**Meeting Frequency**: Weekly for production deployments; On-demand for urgent releases

The ORT ensures that all systems, applications, and infrastructure components are fully prepared for production deployment with appropriate operational support, monitoring, and maintenance procedures.

**See**: [Operational Readiness Test (ORT)](../governing-bodies/operational-readiness-test-review.md) for complete details on composition, readiness criteria, review scope, and validation processes.
page_texts.24:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#35-turnover-to-operations-tops]

### 3.5 Turnover to Operations (TOPS)

**Gate Authority**: Gate 5 - Turnover to Operations Process

**Purpose**: Formal handoff process to operations teams with comprehensive knowledge transfer and operational readiness validation.

**Meeting Frequency**: As needed for production deployments and system transitions

The TOPS process ensures complete and successful transition of systems from development to production operations with full operational support capabilities, including knowledge transfer, documentation review, and monitoring configuration.

**See**: [Turnover to Operations (TOPS)](../governing-bodies/turnover-to-operations.md) for complete details on composition, handoff procedures, entrance criteria, and process activities.
page_texts.25:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#36-post-project-review-ppr]

### 3.6 Post Project Review (PPR)

**Gate Authority**: Gate 6 - Post Project Review Process

**Purpose**: Retrospective evaluation of project outcomes, lessons learned documentation, and continuous improvement.

**Meeting Frequency**: Scheduled 30-90 days after Product Go Live

The PPR conducts comprehensive evaluation of project outcomes, business value realization, and process effectiveness, ensuring lessons learned are captured and incorporated into future projects and governance processes.

**See**: [Post Project Review (PPR)](../governing-bodies/post-project-review.md) for complete details on composition, review scope, outcome assessment, and continuous improvement processes.

---

[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#40-committees]

## 4.0 Committees

The governance framework includes specialized committees that provide expert review, recommendations, and guidance to support consistent decision-making across the enterprise. Detailed information about each committee, including composition, responsibilities, review processes, and meeting structures, is documented in the [Committees](../committees/README.md) section.
page_texts.27:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#41-sales-review-committee]

### 4.1 Sales Review Committee

**Purpose**: Provides technical review and architectural guidance for sales opportunities, ensuring proposed solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, capabilities, and strategic direction.

**Meeting Frequency**: Weekly (or ad-hoc as needed for urgent opportunities)

The Sales Review Committee conducts rapid technical review of sales opportunities, providing feasibility assessment, risk identification, and architectural guidance to support sales efforts.

**See**: [Sales Review Committee](../committees/sales-review-committee.md) for complete details on composition, advisory criteria, review process, and responsibilities.
page_texts.28:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#42-standards-review-committee]

### 4.2 Standards Review Committee

**Purpose**: Reviews and approves Enterprise Architecture Standards across all domains, ensuring technical quality, governance compliance, and alignment with enterprise architecture principles.

**Meeting Frequency**: Bi-weekly (or as needed based on standards submission volume)

The Standards Review Committee provides independent technical review and approval of Enterprise Architecture Standards, ensuring consistency and quality across all architecture domains.

**See**: [Standards Review Committee](../committees/standards-review-committee.md) for complete details on composition, review process, criteria, and responsibilities.
page_texts.29:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#43-technology-review-committee]

### 4.3 Technology Review Committee

**Purpose**: Evaluates and recommends technology platforms, tools, and solutions for enterprise adoption, ensuring alignment with enterprise architecture standards and strategic direction.

**Meeting Frequency**: Monthly (or as needed based on technology evaluation requests)

The Technology Review Committee conducts comprehensive evaluation of proposed technologies, maintains the enterprise technology radar, and provides recommendations (Adopt/Trial/Assess/Hold) for technology adoption.

**See**: [Technology Review Committee](../committees/technology-review-committee.md) for complete details on composition, evaluation criteria, technology radar, and review process.
page_texts.30:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#44-adr-review-committee]

### 4.4 ADR Review Committee

**Purpose**: Reviews and approves Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) across all domains, ensuring technical quality, governance compliance, and alignment with enterprise architecture standards.

**Meeting Frequency**: Bi-weekly (or as needed based on ADR submission volume)

The ADR Review Committee provides independent technical review and approval of Architecture Decision Records, ensuring consistency in architectural decision documentation across domains.

**See**: [ADR Review Committee](../committees/adr-review-committee.md) for complete details on composition, review criteria, process, and responsibilities.

---
page_texts.31:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#50-decision-making-process]

## 5.0 Decision Making Process

The decision-making process ensures systematic evaluation, stakeholder engagement, and proper documentation of all significant architectural decisions.
page_texts.33:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#step-1-proposal-submission]

#### Step 1: Proposal Submission

- **Formal Presentation**: Proposal presentation to Conceptual Review Review Board
- **Business Case**: Clear articulation of business need and expected outcomes
- **Technical Requirements**: Detailed technical specifications and constraints
- **Stakeholder Identification**: Affected parties and required approvals
- **Timeline Requirements**: Implementation deadlines and dependencies
page_texts.34:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#step-2-impact-assessment]

#### Step 2: Impact Assessment

- **Business Impact**: Evaluation of business benefits, risks, and resource requirements
- **Technical Impact**: Assessment of technical complexity, integration requirements, and dependencies
- **Operational Impact**: Analysis of operational procedures, support requirements, and training needs
- **Compliance Impact**: Review of regulatory, security, and policy implications
- **Cost Analysis**: Total cost of ownership including implementation, operation, and maintenance
page_texts.35:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#step-3-stakeholder-review]

#### Step 3: Stakeholder Review

- **Stakeholder Engagement**: Collaboration with affected teams and business units
- **Expert Consultation**: Input from subject matter experts and domain specialists
- **Risk Assessment**: Identification and mitigation planning for identified risks
- **Alternative Analysis**: Evaluation of alternative approaches and solutions
- **Consensus Building**: Facilitated discussions to build stakeholder agreement
page_texts.36:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#step-4-arb-review]

#### Step 4: ARB Review

- **Formal Presentation**: Proposal presentation to Architecture Review Board
- **Technical Deep Dive**: Detailed technical review and questioning
- **Business Alignment**: Verification of alignment with business strategy and objectives
- **Decision Criteria**: Application of established evaluation criteria and standards
- **Final Decision**: Formal approval, conditional approval, or rejection with feedback
page_texts.37:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#step-5-implementation-planning]

#### Step 5: Implementation Planning

- **Implementation Roadmap**: Development of detailed implementation plan and timeline
- **Resource Planning**: Allocation of required resources and team assignments
- **Risk Mitigation**: Implementation of identified risk mitigation strategies
- **Communication Plan**: Stakeholder communication and change management approach
- **Success Metrics**: Definition of success criteria and measurement approaches
page_texts.38:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#step-6-operation-readiness-test-ort]

#### Step 6: Operation Readiness Test (ORT)

- **Security Review**: Comprehensive security assessment and compliance verification
- **Hosting Review**: Infrastructure readiness and capacity verification
- **Performance Testing**: System performance validation and optimization
- **Documentation Review**: Completeness of operational documentation and procedures
- **Training Completion**: Verification of required training and knowledge transfer
page_texts.39:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#step-7-turnover-to-operations-tops]

#### Step 7: Turnover to Operations (TOPS)

- **Operational Handoff**: Formal transfer to operations team with complete documentation
- **Support Procedures**: Establishment of ongoing support and maintenance procedures
- **Monitoring Setup**: Implementation of operational monitoring and alerting
- **Knowledge Transfer**: Complete knowledge transfer to support teams
- **Production Go Live**: Authorization for production deployment and go-live
page_texts.40:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#step-8-post-project-review-ppr]

#### Step 8: Post Project Review (PPR)

- **Outcome Assessment**: Evaluation of business value realization and success metrics
- **Process Evaluation**: Review of governance process effectiveness and efficiency
- **Lessons Learned**: Comprehensive documentation of project insights and recommendations
- **Continuous Improvement**: Identification of governance and process improvement opportunities
- **Project Closure**: Formal project closure and knowledge transfer to organization
page_texts.41:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#step-9-communication-and-follow-up]

#### Step 9: Communication and Follow-up

- **Decision Communication**: Broadcast decisions and rationale to organization
- **Implementation Tracking**: Progress monitoring and issue resolution
- **Best Practices**: Integration of lessons learned into organizational knowledge base
- **Continuous Improvement**: Process refinement based on experience and feedback
page_texts.42:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#52-review-criteria]

### 5.2 Review Criteria

All architectural decisions are evaluated against these standard criteria:
page_texts.43:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#business-alignment]

#### Business Alignment

- **Strategic Fit**: Alignment with enterprise strategy and business objectives
- **Value Delivery**: Clear articulation of business value and return on investment
- **Stakeholder Support**: Demonstrated business stakeholder engagement and support
- **Timeline Alignment**: Compatibility with business timeline and milestone requirements
page_texts.44:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#technical-excellence]

#### Technical Excellence

- **Architectural Soundness**: Adherence to architectural principles and best practices
- **Technical Feasibility**: Realistic assessment of technical implementation complexity
- **Integration Compatibility**: Seamless integration with existing systems and platforms
- **Scalability and Performance**: Ability to meet current and future performance requirements
page_texts.45:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#risk-management]

#### Risk Management

- **Risk Identification**: Comprehensive identification of technical, business, and operational risks
- **Mitigation Planning**: Clear strategies for risk mitigation and contingency planning
- **Security Compliance**: Adherence to security standards and regulatory requirements
- **Operational Impact**: Minimal disruption to existing operations and services
page_texts.46:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#resource-optimization]

#### Resource Optimization

- **Cost Effectiveness**: Optimal use of financial and human resources
- **Resource Availability**: Realistic assessment of required skills and team capacity
- **Reusability**: Opportunities for component reuse and standardization
- **Maintenance Efficiency**: Long-term maintainability and operational efficiency
page_texts.48:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#decision-documentation]

#### Decision Documentation

- **ADR Creation**: Formal Architecture Decision Records created for:
  - Decisions within ARB scope (solution architectures, technology selections, standards changes, integration patterns, vendor selections, compliance exceptions)
  - Decisions with enterprise-wide impact affecting multiple systems or domains
  - Decisions involving significant trade-offs where alternatives were evaluated
  - Decisions that are difficult or expensive to reverse
  - Decisions that establish precedents for future architectural choices
- **Stakeholder Notification**: Timely communication to all affected stakeholders
- **Implementation Guidelines**: Clear guidance for development and operations teams
- **Training Materials**: Educational content for knowledge transfer and adoption
page_texts.49:
[governance/processes/architecture-governance.md#implementation-support]

#### Implementation Support

- **Technical Assistance**: Ongoing architectural guidance during implementation
- **Issue Resolution**: Rapid response to implementation challenges and questions
- **Quality Assurance**: Regular review checkpoints and quality validation
- **Success Measurement**: Tracking of implementation success and business outcomes

---
